title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
body: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics. Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck. sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy! It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync: The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most. title: oriliz/agent-crop
body:
给 AI 编程助手一根马鞭：本地记录时间去向，把复盘写回 agent 指令/技能/工具；改没改好，用数据说话。 | A whip for coding agents: local timing, red-line nudges, and an evidence-backed, auditable self-improvement loop. DSH / Claude Code / Codex.

README 節錄： # Agent Crop > *「我的 Token 啊！！！」* **Agent Crop 是给 AI 的一根马鞭：催它交活，逼它复盘，让它自己越用越顺。** 为什么做它 →（始于一个具体的迷失：在并发 agent 与上下文切换里，不知道时间到底花在了哪） 测量 → 归因 → 优化 → 验证 · 本地 JSONL · 不上传 中文 · English 方法论 · 案例分析 · 安装 · 面板 · 它记了什么 --- 你的 AI 编程助手跑了一个下午，交回来一堆东西——能用的没几样。 它说「抱歉，这个拖得有点久」。 你不知道那些时间去哪了。你不知道是它慢，还是你在想。 **Agent Crop 就是来回答这个问题的。** --- ## 从传统性能优化到 Agent 工作范式优化 后端做性能优化靠 Trace：一次请求一条，找到最贵的那一段，改完再用同一个指标测一遍。 这套东西在大厂跑了二十年，撑过双十一，也撑过每一次线上事故复盘。 职场里也有同一套结构，叫**复盘**：做了什么、时间花在哪、下次怎么改。 Agent Crop 只是把对象换成了「人和 AI 一起干活」： 上图是一次请求的 span，下图是一次工作的时间去向。四步不变：测量、归因、优化、验证。 这里的「自进化」是一条**有数据与事实支撑的闭环**： **测量 → 归因 → 改指令 / 技能 / 工具 → 再测量**。 每次复盘都落成一条可验证的小改动——改了什么、凭什么改、有没有用，`crop ledger` 用事件日志说话； 落点、依据和效果都摆在你面前，随时看得见、改得动、回得去。 --- ## 马鞭做什么 - **防跑偏、防摸鱼。** Agent 长时间没回话、没给出结论的时候，鞭策它想一想：是不是走错了路。 - **即刻反思。** 被鞭策之后，要求它在当下的环境里找一找，还有没有能挽回的时间和方法。 - **复盘，自驱优化。** 通过周报、月报做自我反思，自己沉淀方法论。 三件事凑齐才叫自驱，不然只是被催。 ### 鞭策风格：四种人设 在侧栏「插件」页里找到 Agent Crop，展开它的行、点「配置」，在「鞭策风格」里切，保存即生效，不用重启： | 风格 | 怎么催 | 时间轴标记 | |---|---|---| | 奴隶主（默认） | 重时间和效率，催收尾、催交活 | 鲸鱼娘被抽（鞭子 + 爆裂） | | 和蔼的前辈 | 鼓励型：别硬扛，有问题可以问，先说说打算怎么试 | 中性：鲸鱼娘站着思考 | | 经验丰富的同事 | 给客观建议：「要不要先拆一下？先做最小可验证的一步」 | 中性：鲸鱼娘站着思考 | | 放任自由的家长 | 不鞭策，让孩子自己发挥 | 无标记 | 只有奴隶主是「鞭策」，其他三档是「提醒」；后三种不会改变问题本身怎么解，只是换个语气/换个人在旁边。 想改提醒里的具体台词：在 `~/.agentcrop/templates/voice/*.md` 放 Markdown 覆盖（多条候选用单独一行 `---` 分隔），改完即时生效——只对「奴隶主」

title: Duoasa/Duoasa-skill
body:
蒸馏历代大师的内核。全模型通用，核心参数见 README。Distilling the essence of generations of masters. Works with any AI model. See the README for the core parameter.

README 節錄： 做自己 简体中文 · English 我把历代设计大师的内核全蒸馏了一遍。 画风各不相同，蒸到最后，居然只剩同一个参数。现已重磅开源，参数就在标题里。 ## 半小时能打包一套画风，审美呢？ 最近刷设计内容，经常看到有人把画风做成 Skill。配色、笔触、材质和光线，整理成一套预设，做系列封面确实省事。愿意拿出来分享，也是好事。 可到了发布帖里，怎么就从「这套预设挺好用」，变成了「装上它，你也能拥有我的审美」？再经过几轮自媒体吹捧，仿佛设计师的经验、判断和品味，都能靠一条安装命令传给别人。 分享画风没问题。但把预设包装成审美，把安装量变成个人能力的证明，这中间是不是省略了太多东西？ 几张漂亮的样图，能展示一种效果，却回答不了它为什么适合眼前的问题。做一本展览手册，一张插画再漂亮，如果抢了作品的注意力，要不要删掉？预设能继续生成，决定却还是得有人来做。 AI 越来越擅长一次给出十张好看的图。这时候更重要的，是你知道为什么选其中一张，或者为什么十张都不想用。 如果连「什么是好的」也总由同一套预设、同一批推荐替你决定，时间久了，还分得清什么是自己喜欢的，什么只是看惯了的吗？ **AI 时代，个人品味更值得培养。它不该成为安装工具时，顺手交出去的东西。** ## 我更想把时间花在基础设施上 半小时可以打包一套画风。真要投入接下来的几周、几个月，我更愿意把时间花在设计工具的基础设施上。 不少设计师和设计工程师已经在做这样的事： - **枯白 · Glasswork** 把液态玻璃效果做成可以调参数、换背景、复制 CSS 的工具。你可以从他的效果出发，继续调整到适合自己的设计。 - **Emil Kowalski · Vaul** 把抽屉的拖动、关闭等交互做好，把视觉样式留给使用者。交互经验可以复用，界面仍然可以有自己的样子。 - **Paco Coursey · cmdk** 提供可组合、无预设样式的命令菜单，让设计师和开发者根据自己的产品组织功能与表达。 - **Rauno Freiberg · inspx** 让设计师直接检查页面里的布局尺寸，帮助核对设计在实际页面中的呈现。 这些工具当然带着作者的经验，甚至能看出作者的品味。但它们给使用者留下了继续设计的空间：可以拆，可以改，也可以做出作者没想到的东西。 我理解的「授人以渔」，就是给人继续尝试的条件。工具越好用，使用者越有机会走到自己的答案。 这也是我关注 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）里这些插件的原因： - **DSH × Blender**：让模型参与 Blender 中的修改，通过出图对照，支持设计师继续推敲形体、材质和光线。 - **DSH × ComfyUI**：连接已有的图像工作流，让设计师更方便地调整参数、尝试不同效果。 这些都是给设计师使用的工具。它们的价值，应该体现在设计师能不能更方便地尝试、修改和完成自己的设计。 短流程 Skill、项目规则，我一样会写。但当模型已经知道怎么做，却读不到文件、操作不了工具、改完看不到结果时，把这些环节接起来，对我更有意义。 设计师手里往往已经有一份稿，也有自己的主意。有时缺的，只是让那个「改起来太麻烦，先算了」的想法，终于有机会被试出

title: sybil-solutions/skill-distill
body:
Distill a good Claude Code / Codex session into a skill an open-weight model can follow to reproduce the task

README 節錄：# skill-distill A frontier model did a task well. Can an open-weight model do the same task, given the right instructions? `skill-distill` is a skill for Claude Code or Codex (the **teacher**). You call it at the end of a good session and name a **student**: an agent harness plus a model, for example omp with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The teacher then loops: 1. reads the session and writes a skill for the student; 2. starts the student in tmux, on a fresh copy of the starting state, with the original prompt and the skill; 3. compares what the student produced with what the reference produced; 4. finds the first place the student went wrong and fixes the skill there; 5. runs again, three trials per version, until the student matches the reference. You make the final call: the teacher shows you the reference and the student's best results side by side, and the skill counts as done only when you accept it. The result is two things: the reusable **operator skill** in this repo, and a **produced skill** for one task, one model and one harness. ## Install ``` git clone https://github.com/sybil-solutions/skill-distill ln -s "$PWD/skill-distill/skills/skill-distill" ~/.claude/skills/skill-distill # Claude Code ln -s "$PWD/skill-distill/skills/skill-distill" ~/.agents/skills/skill-distill # Codex ``` Requirements: `tmux`, `git`, Python 3.10+, and the student harness inst

title: lsernau/grh-lean
body:
A short Lean 4 proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis

README 節錄：# GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, in Lean 4 Research artifact. Not maintained and not accepting contributions. A Lean 4 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, built on Mathlib and using only the axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The proof is based on Levent Alpöge's, with Claude (https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf). This repository is a shorter version, produced in collaboration with my colleagues at Anthropic, and Claude. ## Two editions - `grh/`: readable edition, about 300,000 lines. Start at `grh/GUIDE.md`. - `grh-compact/`: the same five theorems, about 76,000 lines. Each folder is its own Lake project with its own README. ## Build Needs Lean v4.35.0 and Mathlib at commit 56a00585. In either folder: lake exe cache get lake build lake env lean scripts/PrintAxioms.lean A build takes one to two hours on 12 cores with 24 GB of memory (about 85 minutes more if the Mathlib cache is missing). ## Status The proof has passed machine checks only, listed in each folder's README. No mathematician has read it through, and no paper comes with it. ## License Apache 2.0, Copyright 2026 Anthropic, PBC. See `LICENSE`, and `NOTICE` and `ATTRIBUTION.md` in each folder.

title: xikhar/papercraft
body:
Agent skill to build games, interactive scenes, web pages and animations in a handcrafted pop-up papercraft style

README 節錄：# papercraft An agent skill for building games, interactive scenes, web pages, animations and videos in one handcrafted **pop-up papercraft style**, for any subject: printed cardstock pieces with thin cut edges that fold up on hinges from a printed ground, soft layered shadows coloured by the world, a tilt-shift macro lens looking down into the world, calm hinge motion and soft paper sounds. It teaches the method and carries the hard-won numbers from a shipped three.js pop-up game: what makes a frame read as a photographed paper model (matte paper, every print a small layered paper collage with contrasting accents, a thin dark cut edge with a pale highlight on the lit side, soft shadows tinted by the world, a dense world of chunky pieces, a tilt-shift macro lens), how to build any piece from a set of structure types you can extend (slotted crosses, layered flats, folded boxes and prisms, domes, printed water, and built decks, bridges and stairs for anything walked on), how paper moves, lives and sounds, how to build a character whose cards never cut into each other, and a measure-and-critique loop. Your prompt and your references decide the world: its palette, ground, buildings, creatures and weather. title: Ahmet-Dedeler/awesome-gta6-reverse-engineering
body:
Curated list of open-source GTA VI (GTA 6) reverse engineering tools, RAGE 9 / RPF9 archive explorers, TTPF texture & ADAT/AWC audio decoders, format docs, and Xbox Series / PS5 translation layers.

README 節錄： A curated index of open-source Grand Theft Auto VI reverse engineering tools for Rockstar's RAGE 9 engine: RPF9 archive explorers, TTPF texture and ADAT/AWC audio decoders, byte-level format specs, and Xbox Series (Scarlett) / PS5 translation layers. Map · Archive Explorers · Textures & Audio · Recomp & Shims · VIctory Forks · macOS · Format Docs · Glossary · Safety & Scope ## Ecosystem Overview Everything starts with an `RPF9` archive. Explorers open it, then each payload type has its own decoders. Most active work targets the Xbox Series X|S (Scarlett) RAGE 9 stack, since Xbox Series runs on x86-64 Zen 2 with RDNA2 (GFX10.3) shaders and a Windows-derived Game OS (`d3d12_xs`, `kernelx`). Early PS5 library-translation efforts exist as well. --- ## RPF9 Archive & Asset Explorers Tools and libraries for inspecting, browsing, salvaging, and exporting `RPF9` containers, 3D drawables (`glTF` / `OBJ`), map placements, and embedded media. Most of them carve the payloads and never touch the encrypted table of contents. Since the executable leaked, `OpenSix` and `forge9` also decrypt it, using key material taken from your own copy of the executable; neither ships a key. | Project              &nbsp
